docs.text: Features Route groups During development, developers often need to create sets of visually similar routes. The traditional way is creating each route, one by one, like in the below example: $app->post('/product/create', CreateProductHandler::class, 'product:create'); $app->delete('/product/delete/{id}', DeleteProductHandler::class, 'product:delete'); $app->patch('/product/update/{id}', UpdateProductHandler::class, 'product:update'); $app->get('/product/view/{id}', GetProductHandler::class, 'product:view'); Besides the features provided by mezzio/mezzio-fastroute , dot-router offers route groups, which are collections of routes that (partially) share the same path. To use this feature, first get an instance of the Dot\Router\RouteCollector using the below code: /** @var \Dot\Router\RouteCollectorInterface $routeCollector */ $routeCollector = $container->get(\Dot\Router\RouteCollectorInterface::class); Then rewrite the above routes using the below code: $routeCollector->group('/product') ->post('/create', CreateProductHandler::class, 'product:create'); ->delete('/delete/{id}', DeleteProductHandler::class, 'product:delete'); ->patch('/update/{id}', UpdateProductHandler::class, 'product:update'); ->get('/view/{id}', GetProductHandler::class, 'product:view'); Note that /product becomes the group prefix and the routes only specify part that is specific only to them. When dot-router registers the routes, it will automatically prepend the prefix to each route path. Advantages Dry no need for repeating common route parts encapsulation: similar routes are grouped in a single block of code (vs. each route a separate statement) easy path refactoring: modify all routes at once by changing only the prefix easy copying/moving: copying/moving an entire group makes sure that you don't accidentally omit a route Exclude middleware Besides sharing the same path, sometimes routes may need to share handlers/middlewares too. A good example is the usage presence of CheckOwnerMiddleware in the below example: $app->post('/product/create', CreateProductHandler::class, 'product:create'); $app->delete('/product/delete/{id}', [CheckOwnerMiddleware::class, DeleteProductHandler::class], 'product:delete'); $app->patch('/product/update/{id}', [CheckOwnerMiddleware::class, UpdateProductHandler::class], 'product:update'); $app->get('/product/view/{id}', [CheckOwnerMiddleware::class, GetProductHandler::class], 'product:view'); Just like in the first example, the routes are similar but this time there is CheckOwnerMiddleware , a middleware used by three out of the four routes. For such cases, dot-router provides for specific routes the ability to exclude middleware from their pipeline. Using this feature, we can rewrite the above example like this: $routeCollector->group('/product', CheckOwnerMiddleware::class) ->post('/create', CreateProductHandler::class, 'product:create', CheckOwnerMiddleware::class) ->delete('/delete/{id}', DeleteProductHandler::class, 'product:delete') ->patch('/update/{id}', UpdateProductHandler::class, 'product:update') ->get('/view/{id}', GetProductHandler::class, 'product:view'); Note the second argument of the group method is CheckOwnerMiddleware::class . This way all group middlewares will be prepended to the route's handler, so this is the equivalent of using: $app->post('/product/create', [CheckOwnerMiddleware::class, CreateProductHandler::class], 'product:create') Advantages extends the DRYness of route groups by allowing to specify common middlewares only once per route shorter and easier-to-read route definitions

docs.text: Usage Register routes in your application using your preferred method: in config/routes.php per-module, using a RoutesDelegator Both methods will provide access to the application's container via the $container variable. There are two types of routes that you can create: create a single route create a route group

docs.text: Register routes in your application using your preferred method: in config/routes.php per-module, using a RoutesDelegator Both methods will provide access to the application's container via the $container variable. docs.text: Creating route groups Following this tutorial assumes that you already completed the installation and configuration steps. Access the RouteCollector Get an instance of the Dot\Router\RouteCollector using the below code: /** @var \Dot\Router\RouteCollectorInterface $routeCollector */ $routeCollector = $container->get(\Dot\Router\RouteCollectorInterface::class); Create a route group Create a route group by setting the route group prefix and optionally a(n array of) common middleware(s): $routeCollector->group('/resource', SomeMiddleware::class); group method arguments: prefix : required, a string that will be prepended to each route from the group middleware : optional, (array of) request middleware(s) to execute before the route handler(s) Append a route that matches specific request methods $routeCollector->group('/resource', [SomeMiddleware::class, OtherMiddleware::class]) ->route('/manage', ResourceHandler::class, 'route-name', ['GET', 'POST']); If this route does not need to be piped through specific middleware(s), you can specify the fifth argument $excludeMiddleware exclude those middlewares at route level (makes sense when there are multiple routes in a group): $routeCollector->group('/resource', [SomeMiddleware::class, OtherMiddleware::class]) ->route('/manage', ResourceHandler::class, 'route-name', ['GET', 'POST'], excludeMiddleware: SomeMiddleware::class); route() method arguments: path : required, of type string middleware : required, (array of) request handler(s)/middleware(s) name : (optional) if omitted, it will be set using the pattern route path ^METHOD1:METHOD2 methods : (optional) if omitted, the route will respond to all request methods (equivalent of any() ) excludeMiddleware : (optional) (array of) request handler(s)/middleware(s) to exclude for this route Append a route that matches any request method $routeCollector->group('/resource', [SomeMiddleware::class, OtherMiddleware::class]) ->any('/manage', ResourceHandler::class, 'route-name'); If this route does not need to be piped through specific middleware(s), you can specify the fourth argument $excludeMiddleware exclude those middlewares at route level (makes sense when there are multiple routes in a group): $routeCollector->group('/resource', [SomeMiddleware::class, OtherMiddleware::class]) ->any('/manage', ResourceHandler::class, 'route-name', excludeMiddleware: SomeMiddleware::class); any() method arguments: path : required, of type string middleware : required, (array of) request handler(s)/middleware(s) name : optional, if omitted, it will be set to the value of the route path excludeMiddleware : optional, (array of) request handler(s)/middleware(s) to exclude for this route Append a route that matches DELETE requests $routeCollector->group('/resource', [SomeMiddleware::class, OtherMiddleware::class]) ->delete('/{id}', ResourceHandler::class, 'route-name'); If this route does not need to be piped through specific middleware(s), you can specify the fourth argument $excludeMiddleware exclude those middlewares at route level (makes sense when there are multiple routes in a group): $routeCollector->group('/resource', [SomeMiddleware::class, OtherMiddleware::class]) ->delete('/{id}', ResourceHandler::class, 'route-name', excludeMiddleware: SomeMiddleware::class); delete() method arguments: path : required, of type string middleware : required, (array of) request handler(s)/middleware(s) name : optional, if omitted, it will be set using the pattern route path ^DELETE excludeMiddleware : optional, (array of) request handler(s)/middleware(s) to exclude for this route Append a route that matches GET requests $routeCollector->group('/resource', [SomeMiddleware::class, OtherMiddleware::class]) ->get('/{id}', ResourceHandler::class, 'route-name'); If this route does not need to be piped through specific middleware(s), you can specify the fourth argument $excludeMiddleware exclude those middlewares at route level (makes sense when there are multiple routes in a group): $routeCollector->group('/resource', [SomeMiddleware::class, OtherMiddleware::class]) ->get('/{id}', ResourceHandler::class, 'route-name', excludeMiddleware: SomeMiddleware::class); get() method arguments: path : required, of type string middleware : required, (array of) request handler(s)/middleware(s) name : optional, if omitted, it will be set using the pattern route path ^GET excludeMiddleware : optional, (array of) request handler(s)/middleware(s) to exclude for this route Append a route that matches PATCH requests $routeCollector->group('/resource', [SomeMiddleware::class, OtherMiddleware::class]) ->patch('/{id}', ResourceHandler::class, 'route-name'); If this route does not need to be piped through specific middleware(s), you can specify the fourth argument $excludeMiddleware exclude those middlewares at route level (makes sense when there are multiple routes in a group): $routeCollector->group('/resource', [SomeMiddleware::class, OtherMiddleware::class]) ->patch('/{id}', ResourceHandler::class, 'route-name', excludeMiddleware: SomeMiddleware::class); patch() method arguments: path : required, of type string middleware : required, (array of) request handler(s)/middleware(s) name : optional, if omitted, it will be set using the pattern route path ^PATCH excludeMiddleware : optional, (array of) request handler(s)/middleware(s) to exclude for this route Append a route that matches POST requests $routeCollector->group('/resource', [SomeMiddleware::class, OtherMiddleware::class]) ->post('', ResourceHandler::class, 'route-name'); If this route does not need to be piped through specific middleware(s), you can specify the fourth argument $excludeMiddleware exclude those middlewares at route level (makes sense when there are multiple routes in a group): $routeCollector->group('/resource', [SomeMiddleware::class, OtherMiddleware::class]) ->post('', ResourceHandler::class, 'route-name', excludeMiddleware: SomeMiddleware::class); post() method arguments: path : required, of type string middleware : required, (array of) request handler(s)/middleware(s) name : optional, if omitted, it will be set using the pattern route path ^POST excludeMiddleware : optional, (array of) request handler(s)/middleware(s) to exclude for this route Append a route that matches PUT requests $routeCollector->group('/resource', [SomeMiddleware::class, OtherMiddleware::class]) ->put('/{id}', ResourceHandler::class, 'route-name'); If this route does not need to be piped through specific middleware(s), you can specify the fourth argument $excludeMiddleware exclude those middlewares at route level (makes sense when there are multiple routes in a group): $routeCollector->group('/resource', [SomeMiddleware::class, OtherMiddleware::class]) ->put('/{id}', ResourceHandler::class, 'route-name', excludeMiddleware: SomeMiddleware::class); put() method arguments: path : required, of type string middleware : required, (array of) request handler(s)/middleware(s) name : optional, if omitted, it will be set using the pattern route path ^PUT excludeMiddleware : optional, (array of) request handler(s)/middleware(s) to exclude for this route

docs.text: Features Route groups During development, developers often need to create sets of visually similar routes. The traditional way is creating each route, one by one, like in the below example: $app->post('/product/create', CreateProductHandler::class, 'product:create'); $app->delete('/product/delete/{id}', DeleteProductHandler::class, 'product:delete'); $app->patch('/product/update/{id}', UpdateProductHandler::class, 'product:update'); $app->get('/product/view/{id}', GetProductHandler::class, 'product:view'); Besides the features provided by mezzio/mezzio-fastroute , dot-router offers route groups, which are collections of routes that (partially) share the same path. To use this feature, first get an instance of the Dot\Router\RouteCollector using the below code: /** @var \Dot\Router\RouteCollectorInterface $routeCollector */ $routeCollector = $container->get(\Dot\Router\RouteCollectorInterface::class); Then rewrite the above routes using the below code: $routeCollector->group('/product') ->post('/create', CreateProductHandler::class, 'product:create') ->delete('/delete/{id}', DeleteProductHandler::class, 'product:delete') ->patch('/update/{id}', UpdateProductHandler::class, 'product:update') ->get('/view/{id}', GetProductHandler::class, 'product:view'); Note that /product becomes the group prefix and the routes only specify the part that is specific to them. When dot-router registers the routes, it prepends the prefix to each route path. The prefix and the path are joined as they are, so do not end the prefix with / ( /product/ plus /create gives /product//create ). Advantages Dry no need for repeating common route parts encapsulation: similar routes are grouped in a single block of code (vs. each route a separate statement) easy path refactoring: modify all routes at once by changing only the prefix easy copying/moving: copying/moving an entire group makes sure that you don't accidentally omit a route Group middleware Besides sharing the same path, routes often share middleware too. A good example is CheckOwnerMiddleware in the below example: $app->delete('/product/delete/{id}', [CheckOwnerMiddleware::class, DeleteProductHandler::class], 'product:delete'); $app->patch('/product/update/{id}', [CheckOwnerMiddleware::class, UpdateProductHandler::class], 'product:update'); $app->get('/product/view/{id}', [CheckOwnerMiddleware::class, GetProductHandler::class], 'product:view'); Pass the shared middleware as the second argument of group() , and dot-router runs it before the handler of every route in the group: $routeCollector->group('/product', CheckOwnerMiddleware::class) ->delete('/delete/{id}', DeleteProductHandler::class, 'product:delete') ->patch('/update/{id}', UpdateProductHandler::class, 'product:update') ->get('/view/{id}', GetProductHandler::class, 'product:view'); Group middleware runs first, in the order given, followed by the route's own middleware and handler. This applies to every kind of route handler: class names, objects, closures and other callables. Exclude middleware Sometimes one route in a group must not run a group middleware. In the below example, creating a product has no owner to check yet: $app->post('/product/create', CreateProductHandler::class, 'product:create'); $app->delete('/product/delete/{id}', [CheckOwnerMiddleware::class, DeleteProductHandler::class], 'product:delete'); $app->patch('/product/update/{id}', [CheckOwnerMiddleware::class, UpdateProductHandler::class], 'product:update'); $app->get('/product/view/{id}', [CheckOwnerMiddleware::class, GetProductHandler::class], 'product:view'); For such cases, each group route accepts $excludeMiddleware as its last argument: $routeCollector->group('/product', CheckOwnerMiddleware::class) ->post('/create', CreateProductHandler::class, 'product:create', CheckOwnerMiddleware::class) ->delete('/delete/{id}', DeleteProductHandler::class, 'product:delete') ->patch('/update/{id}', UpdateProductHandler::class, 'product:update') ->get('/view/{id}', GetProductHandler::class, 'product:view'); The product:create route is now the equivalent of: $app->post('/product/create', CreateProductHandler::class, 'product:create'); How exclusion works: $excludeMiddleware is a class name or a list of class names. It removes group middleware only. The route's own middleware and handler always run. A group middleware given as a class name is excluded when that exact name is listed. A group middleware given as an object is excluded when it is an instance of a listed class or interface. Advantages extends the DRYness of route groups by allowing to specify common middlewares only once per group shorter and easier-to-read route definitions

docs.text: Upgrading from version 1 to version 2 Version 2 drops PHP 8.2, fixes how group middleware is applied, and makes the middleware container follow PSR-11. Most applications only need to update PHP and run composer update ; read the table below if your routes use groups with closures or $excludeMiddleware . Update the package composer require dotkernel/dot-router:^2.0 Changes that can break your code Change Symptom Fix PHP 8.2 support removed Composer refuses to install version 2 Use PHP 8.3 or newer, or stay on version 1 mezzio/mezzio-fastroute minimum is ^3.15 Composer reports a conflict with an older FastRoute version Update mezzio/mezzio-fastroute Callable route handlers in a group now run the group middleware A closure route inside a group now runs, for example, the group's authentication middleware This is usually what you want. To keep the old behaviour, list the group middleware in that route's $excludeMiddleware $excludeMiddleware removes group middleware only Listing the route's own handler or middleware class no longer removes it from the route Remove the class from the route's middleware list instead $excludeMiddleware matches middleware objects by class A group middleware passed as an object is now excluded by its class name; excluding MiddlewareInterface::class removes every group middleware object, but never the route handler Check routes that exclude interface names MiddlewareContainer::get() throws MissingMiddlewareException or InvalidMiddlewareException Code that compares the exception class with Exception::class no longer matches Catch Psr\Container\ContainerExceptionInterface ; both new classes extend RuntimeException , so catch (Exception $e) still works An unregistered middleware class with required constructor arguments throws InvalidMiddlewareException The error was an ArgumentCountError Register the middleware in the container MiddlewareFactory::pipeline() and prepare([]) reject an empty list Dot\Router\Exception\InvalidArgumentException when routes are registered; version 1 raised a PHP warning and registered a route that did nothing Pass at least one middleware or handler A group route with an empty prefix and an empty path is rejected Dot\Router\Exception\InvalidArgumentException Set a prefix or a path Stricter PHPDoc types ( non-empty-string paths and names, list<string> methods) Static analysis of your code reports new errors on route calls Pass non-empty literals, or narrow your variables before the call Group middleware with closures Before, the closure route skipped AuthMiddleware : $routeCollector->group('/admin', AuthMiddleware::class) ->get('/status', fn ($request, $handler) => new JsonResponse(['ok' => true]), 'admin:status'); After, AuthMiddleware runs first for /admin/status , as it does for every other route in the group. To keep the route public, exclude the middleware: $routeCollector->group('/admin', AuthMiddleware::class) ->get('/status', fn ($request, $handler) => new JsonResponse(['ok' => true]), 'admin:status', AuthMiddleware::class); Excluding middleware objects Before, a group middleware passed as an object could not be excluded by its class name: $routeCollector->group('/product', new CheckOwnerMiddleware($repository)) ->post('/create', CreateProductHandler::class, 'product:create', CheckOwnerMiddleware::class); // version 1: CheckOwnerMiddleware still ran // version 2: CheckOwnerMiddleware is skipped for product:create

docs.text: Usage Register routes in your application using your preferred method: in config/routes.php per-module, using a RoutesDelegator Both methods will provide access to the application's container via the $container variable. There are two types of routes that you can create: create a single route create a route group

docs.text: Register routes in your application using your preferred method: in config/routes.php per-module, using a RoutesDelegator Both methods will provide access to the application's container via the $container variable. There are two types of routes that you can create: create a single route create a route group
docs.title: Usage

docs.text: Creating route groups Following this tutorial assumes that you already completed the installation and configuration steps. Access the RouteCollector Get an instance of the Dot\Router\RouteCollector using the below code: /** @var \Dot\Router\RouteCollectorInterface $routeCollector */ $routeCollector = $container->get(\Dot\Router\RouteCollectorInterface::class); Create a route group Create a route group by setting the route group prefix and optionally a(n array of) common middleware(s): $routeCollector->group('/resource', SomeMiddleware::class); group method arguments: prefix : required, a string that will be prepended to each route from the group; do not end it with / middleware : optional, (array of) request middleware(s) to execute before the handler of every route in the group, including closures and other callables Each call to group() returns a new group. Create groups this way rather than fetching Dot\Router\RouteGroupCollectorInterface from the container: the container returns the same shared instance every time, so its prefix and middleware would leak between modules. Which middleware is excluded $excludeMiddleware removes group middleware only; the route's own middleware and handler always run. A group middleware given as a class name is excluded when that exact name is listed. A group middleware given as an object is excluded when it is an instance of a listed class or interface. Append a route that matches specific request methods $routeCollector->group('/resource', [SomeMiddleware::class, OtherMiddleware::class]) ->route('/manage', ResourceHandler::class, 'route-name', ['GET', 'POST']); If this route does not need to be piped through specific middleware(s), you can use the fifth argument, $excludeMiddleware , to exclude those group middlewares at route level (makes sense when there are multiple routes in a group): $routeCollector->group('/resource', [SomeMiddleware::class, OtherMiddleware::class]) ->route('/manage', ResourceHandler::class, 'route-name', ['GET', 'POST'], excludeMiddleware: SomeMiddleware::class); route() method arguments: path : required, of type string middleware : required, (array of) request handler(s)/middleware(s) name : (optional) if omitted, it will be set using the pattern route path ^METHOD1:METHOD2 methods : (optional) if omitted, the route will respond to all request methods (equivalent of any() ) excludeMiddleware : (optional) class name, or list of class names, of group middleware to skip for this route Append a route that matches any request method $routeCollector->group('/resource', [SomeMiddleware::class, OtherMiddleware::class]) ->any('/manage', ResourceHandler::class, 'route-name'); If this route does not need to be piped through specific middleware(s), you can use the fourth argument, $excludeMiddleware , to exclude those group middlewares at route level (makes sense when there are multiple routes in a group): $routeCollector->group('/resource', [SomeMiddleware::class, OtherMiddleware::class]) ->any('/manage', ResourceHandler::class, 'route-name', excludeMiddleware: SomeMiddleware::class); any() method arguments: path : required, of type string middleware : required, (array of) request handler(s)/middleware(s) name : optional, if omitted, it will be set to the value of the route path excludeMiddleware : optional, class name, or list of class names, of group middleware to skip for this route Append a route that matches DELETE requests $routeCollector->group('/resource', [SomeMiddleware::class, OtherMiddleware::class]) ->delete('/{id}', ResourceHandler::class, 'route-name'); If this route does not need to be piped through specific middleware(s), you can use the fourth argument, $excludeMiddleware , to exclude those group middlewares at route level (makes sense when there are multiple routes in a group): $routeCollector->group('/resource', [SomeMiddleware::class, OtherMiddleware::class]) ->delete('/{id}', ResourceHandler::class, 'route-name', excludeMiddleware: SomeMiddleware::class); delete() method arguments: path : required, of type string middleware : required, (array of) request handler(s)/middleware(s) name : optional, if omitted, it will be set using the pattern route path ^DELETE excludeMiddleware : optional, class name, or list of class names, of group middleware to skip for this route Append a route that matches GET requests $routeCollector->group('/resource', [SomeMiddleware::class, OtherMiddleware::class]) ->get('/{id}', ResourceHandler::class, 'route-name'); If this route does not need to be piped through specific middleware(s), you can use the fourth argument, $excludeMiddleware , to exclude those group middlewares at route level (makes sense when there are multiple routes in a group): $routeCollector->group('/resource', [SomeMiddleware::class, OtherMiddleware::class]) ->get('/{id}', ResourceHandler::class, 'route-name', excludeMiddleware: SomeMiddleware::class); get() method arguments: path : required, of type string middleware : required, (array of) request handler(s)/middleware(s) name : optional, if omitted, it will be set using the pattern route path ^GET excludeMiddleware : optional, class name, or list of class names, of group middleware to skip for this route Append a route that matches PATCH requests $routeCollector->group('/resource', [SomeMiddleware::class, OtherMiddleware::class]) ->patch('/{id}', ResourceHandler::class, 'route-name'); If this route does not need to be piped through specific middleware(s), you can use the fourth argument, $excludeMiddleware , to exclude those group middlewares at route level (makes sense when there are multiple routes in a group): $routeCollector->group('/resource', [SomeMiddleware::class, OtherMiddleware::class]) ->patch('/{id}', ResourceHandler::class, 'route-name', excludeMiddleware: SomeMiddleware::class); patch() method arguments: path : required, of type string middleware : required, (array of) request handler(s)/middleware(s) name : optional, if omitted, it will be set using the pattern route path ^PATCH excludeMiddleware : optional, class name, or list of class names, of group middleware to skip for this route Append a route that matches POST requests $routeCollector->group('/resource', [SomeMiddleware::class, OtherMiddleware::class]) ->post('', ResourceHandler::class, 'route-name'); If this route does not need to be piped through specific middleware(s), you can use the fourth argument, $excludeMiddleware , to exclude those group middlewares at route level (makes sense when there are multiple routes in a group): $routeCollector->group('/resource', [SomeMiddleware::class, OtherMiddleware::class]) ->post('', ResourceHandler::class, 'route-name', excludeMiddleware: SomeMiddleware::class); post() method arguments: path : required, of type string middleware : required, (array of) request handler(s)/middleware(s) name : optional, if omitted, it will be set using the pattern route path ^POST excludeMiddleware : optional, class name, or list of class names, of group middleware to skip for this route Append a route that matches PUT requests $routeCollector->group('/resource', [SomeMiddleware::class, OtherMiddleware::class]) ->put('/{id}', ResourceHandler::class, 'route-name'); If this route does not need to be piped through specific middleware(s), you can use the fourth argument, $excludeMiddleware , to exclude those group middlewares at route level (makes sense when there are multiple routes in a group): $routeCollector->group('/resource', [SomeMiddleware::class, OtherMiddleware::class]) ->put('/{id}', ResourceHandler::class, 'route-name', excludeMiddleware: SomeMiddleware::class); put() method arguments: path : required, of type string middleware : required, (array of) request handler(s)/middleware(s) name : optional, if omitted, it will be set using the pattern route path ^PUT excludeMiddleware : optional, class name, or list of class names, of group middleware to skip for this route List the registered routes getRoutes() on a group returns every route registered in the application's route collector, not only the routes of that group.

docs.text: Creating a single route Following this tutorial assumes that you already completed the installation and configuration steps. Access the RouteCollector Get an instance of the Dot\Router\RouteCollector using the below code: /** @var \Dot\Router\RouteCollectorInterface $routeCollector */ $routeCollector = $container->get(\Dot\Router\RouteCollectorInterface::class); Create a route that matches specific request methods $routeCollector->route('/resource/manage', SomeHandler::class, 'route-name', ['GET', 'POST']); route() method arguments: path : required, a non-empty string middleware : required, (array of) request handler(s)/middleware(s) name : (optional) if omitted, it will be set using the pattern route path ^METHOD1:METHOD2 methods : (optional) if omitted, the route will respond to all request methods Create a route that matches any request method $routeCollector->any('/resource/manage', SomeHandler::class, 'route-name'); any() method arguments: path : required, a non-empty string middleware : required, (array of) request handler(s)/middleware(s) name : optional, if omitted, it will be set to the value of the route path Create a route that matches DELETE requests $routeCollector->delete('/resource/{id}', SomeHandler::class, 'route-name'); delete() method arguments: path : required, a non-empty string middleware : required, (array of) request handler(s)/middleware(s) name : optional, if omitted, it will be set using the pattern route path ^DELETE Create a route that matches GET requests $routeCollector->get('/resource/{id}', SomeHandler::class, 'route-name'); get() method arguments: path : required, a non-empty string middleware : required, (array of) request handler(s)/middleware(s) name : optional, if omitted, it will be set using the pattern route path ^GET Create a route that matches PATCH requests $routeCollector->patch('/resource/{id}', SomeHandler::class, 'route-name'); patch() method arguments: path : required, a non-empty string middleware : required, (array of) request handler(s)/middleware(s) name : optional, if omitted, it will be set using the pattern route path ^PATCH Create a route that matches POST requests $routeCollector->post('/resource', SomeHandler::class, 'route-name'); post() method arguments: path : required, a non-empty string middleware : required, (array of) request handler(s)/middleware(s) name : optional, if omitted, it will be set using the pattern route path ^POST Create a route that matches PUT requests $routeCollector->put('/resource/{id}', SomeHandler::class, 'route-name'); put() method arguments: path : required, a non-empty string middleware : required, (array of) request handler(s)/middleware(s) name : optional, if omitted, it will be set using the pattern route path ^PUT Chain routes to the RouteCollector To facilitate creating routes, each $routeCollector method returns the existing RouteCollector instance, so you can chain routes like this: $routeCollector ->route('/product', SomeHandler::class, 'app::product', ['GET', 'POST']) ->any('/category', SomeHandler::class, 'app::category') ->delete('/order/{id}', SomeHandler::class, 'app::delete-order') ->get('/order/{id}', SomeHandler::class, 'app::view-order') ->patch('/order/{id}', SomeHandler::class, 'app::update-order') ->post('/order', SomeHandler::class, 'app::create-order') ->put('/order/{id}', SomeHandler::class, 'app::replace-order');
